name: mruby guest
description: The state every invocation starts from, and what a raise inside a capability gem's frame costs.

scenarios.title: Two invocations begin from the same state, not merely a clean one
given: a Sandbox that has evaluated `Object.new.object_id` once
scenarios.when: the same source is evaluated again
scenarios.then: the same object id comes back

scenarios.title: A constant an invocation defines is gone at the next entry
given: a Sandbox whose evaluation defined a constant
scenarios.when: a later invocation asks whether that constant is defined

scenarios.title: A raise in an output coercion is the guest's error, not the Sandbox's
given: guest source defining a class whose `to_s` raises
an instance of it passed to `$stdout.puts`

scenarios.title: The guest's own message survives the coercion frame
given: guest source defining a class whose `to_s` raises
an instance of it passed to `$stdout.puts`
scenarios.then: the raised error carries the guest exception's message

scenarios.title: The second coercion entry answers like the first
given: guest source defining a class whose `inspect` raises
an instance of it passed to `p`

scenarios.title: The guest's own message survives the inspect frame too
given: guest source defining a class whose `inspect` raises
an instance of it passed to `p`
scenarios.then: the raised error carries the guest exception's message

scenarios.title: A raising callback costs the Sandbox nothing
given: a Sandbox whose invocation failed on a raising output coercion
scenarios.when: a later invocation evaluates ordinary guest source

text: Two invocations of one artifact begin from the same interpreter state, not
merely from a clean one. The heap-slot replay is what settles the difference:
an interpreter that reset everything correctly but started somewhere new each
time would pass every leak test and fail this one.
A capability gem servicing one guest operation calls back into guest code, and
the raise that call may produce has to stay a guest exception. The two coercion
entries are witnessed separately because they are separate frames, and the
recovery scenario is what tells a guest error apart from a retired Sandbox.
That the boot state may be computed at build time, and that per-invocation
resources may be provisioned ahead of demand, are both stated to be
unobservable, so neither is a scenario. The reproducible-build check holds the
baking end. Leak-freedom between invocations is per-invocation isolation and
belongs with the Sandbox behaviors, whose witnesses cite it alongside this one.
